key_insight: Disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion favor dense Fe-based amorphous coatings, while lower porosity improves long-term corrosion resistance and higher humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray parameters and accounting for service humidity can help tailor protective coatings for Q235 carbon steel.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, lamellar structure, and coating porosity.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and sliding wear under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases.
watch_item: The humidity-dependent wear findings involve Si3N4 counterface balls and may not transfer directly to other contact materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
